items.title: Kenny Davern interviewed by Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, September 23, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I heard a concert from I think it was either Carnegie Hall or Lincoln Center with Wynton Marsalis

ctx.x: I wanted to ask you, you talked about Coltrane and of course his main innovation is what we call the sheets of sound, to the place where, and of course he began to go off into the free jazz movement and all that. What is happening now in jazz? Is there any movement now that you see in any way that is equal to any of the great artists or great movements that have shaped jazz in the past? Or is it at a standstill?

I think you said it, it’s at a standstill. It’s perhaps in a state perhaps of decomposition because the other night I heard, again, airport to home and scan the airwaves, I heard a concert from I think it was either Carnegie Hall or Lincoln Center with Wynton Marsalis and they were playing the music of Jelly Roll Morton, which is what I cut my eyeteeth on so to speak when I was growing up. And I mean I really love that music. I could tell you the alternate takes you know, that kind of thing, that’s how engrained…

this particular thing. And then they play one that was with a couple of flubs a couple of goofs and which is not bad, but, it didn’t have exact placement in the articulation of that particular, those notes. And to make up this masterpiece that deservedly belongs to be raved about, but, they’d go and they’d decimate that too by a take that wouldn’t grab the young kid that let’s say I was, today coming along, and it wouldn’t grab him, it wouldn’t send out the message that that original one did.

items.title: Kenny Davern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: That’s what I mean, Wynton comes on, “roux.”

ctx.x: Now see, I thought I wasn’t going ask about it but—

That’s what I mean, Wynton comes on, “roux.” There’s a chapter in the first one, it’s called R-O-U-X, and it actually says, and there he is, cute as a button you know. “Now you could have all kinds of ingredients, you’re going to make a gumbo see? But you
could have them all in there, but if you don’t have roux, you don’t have gumbo, you have gumbo soup, heh, heh, heh” [scats].
